(Search snippet + BBC morning article — approved carriers' reporting language)
A fast-moving wildfire that erupted in the Var department in southern France on Tuesday has burned more than 2,500 hectares and forced about 400 people to flee; the blaze near Draguignan (Taradeau, Les Arcs-sur-Argens, Cotignac) has been brought under control. 10 homes destroyed, 50 damaged; two firefighters and two civilians injured; 2,300 households left without power.
Two professional firefighters, aged 34, died on Tuesday tackling a blaze less than 2km from Bordeaux-Merignac airport in Merignac, Gironde. President Macron expressed condolences and said France had not seen so many blazes since the Second World War, with nearly 11,000 fires this year.
European Forest Fire Information System (Effis) satellite data: more than 42,000 hectares burned in France Jan-mid-July, surpassing the 2022 record — about four times the size of Paris. Spain has also lost tens of thousands of hectares with deaths reported.
